title: Connected clopen support over its field of constants
statement: Let k₀ be a finite field, ℓ an invertible prime, X a smooth affine finite-type k₀-scheme, and V a nonzero arithmetically simple lisse source Weil sheaf [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex, def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let x,y be finite points with nonzero V-stalks. There exist a finite field extension k₁/k₀, a geometrically connected smooth affine separated finite-type k₁-scheme C of constant relative dimension d ≥ 0, and a clopen immersion c:C→X over k₁/k₀. Both x and y lift to finite points of C. No functor on Weil sheaves and no positivity of d is asserted.

proof.text: Since X is finite type and affine over a field, its space is Noetherian. The connected component U of x is therefore open and closed. The clopen-support lemma puts y in U. Its clopen immersion into affine X makes U affine and connected.

proof.text: Apply the connected smooth affine constant-field theorem to U over k0. It constructs the finite constant field k1 and a smooth geometrically connected structure g on the very same scheme U, with the required factorization.

proof.text: On the connected smooth scheme U the relative dimension is constant. Explicitly, regularity makes it irreducible; any two nonempty standard-smooth neighborhoods intersect and their dimensions agree by the dimension comparison over a field. Glue the local smooth-relative-dimension structures. Affineness gives separatedness and quasi-compactness, smoothness gives finite type, and the open immersion preserves the residue fields of the marked points. Transport ring characteristic along the algebra map.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_geometrically_connected_clopen_support
    {k₀ : Type u} [Field k₀] [Finite k₀] {l : ℕ} [Fact l.Prime]
    [Fact (ringChar k₀ ≠ l)] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))] [IsAffine X]
    [Smooth (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))]
    [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))]
    (V : WeilSheaf k₀ l X) (hV : V.IsIrreducibleLisse)
    (x y : X.finitePoints)
    (hx : Nontrivial (V.stalk x).carrier) (hy : Nontrivial (V.stalk y).carrier) :
    ∃ (k₁ : Type u) (_ : Field k₁) (_ : Finite k₁) (_ : Algebra k₀ k₁)
      (_ : Fact (ringChar k₁ ≠ l)) (d : ℕ) (C : Scheme.{u})
      (_ : C.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k₁))) (_ : IsAffine C)
      (_ : SmoothOfRelativeDimension d (C ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₁)))
      (_ : GeometricallyConnected (C ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₁)))
      (_ : IsSeparated (C ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₁)))
      (_ : LocallyOfFiniteType (C ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₁)))
      (_ : QuasiCompact (C ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₁)))
      (c : C ⟶ X) (_ : IsOpenImmersion c) (_ : IsClosedImmersion c),
      c ≫ (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀)) =
        (C ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₁)) ≫
          Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k₀ k₁)) ∧
      ∃ s t : C.finitePoints, c s.1 = x.1 ∧ c t.1 = y.1
